_meta.basis: Register taxonomy per the GPGPU Arch 07 - NVIDIA Ampere deep dive slides: RX general, URX uniform, SRX special, PX predicate, UPX uniform predicate, c[X][Y] constant memory.
_meta.palette_rule: Warm hues mark per-thread (divergent) state; cool hues mark warp-uniform state. That is the single distinction worth seeing instantly when reading SASS.

vector.title: Vector register (per-thread)
vector.desc: One of the general-purpose registers `R0`-`R254`. **Every lane in the warp holds its own copy** - this is per-thread, divergent state, the SASS equivalent of an AMD VGPR. The register file is 256 KB per SM, split into four 64 KB partitions, one per SM sub-partition, so register pressure translates directly into occupancy.

vectorZero.title: RZ - zero register
vectorZero.desc: Reads as 0 and discards anything written to it. It is not a real register: as a source it is the constant zero (`IMAD.MOV.U32 Rd, RZ, RZ, x` is a move), and as a destination it means *compute this for the side effect and throw the value away* - which is exactly what a compare that only needs its predicate output does.

uniform.title: Uniform register (scalar, warp-wide)
uniform.desc: One of `UR0`-`UR63`. **One value shared by the whole warp**, held in a separate small register file and fed by its own uniform datapath. Introduced with Turing to keep warp-invariant work - address bases, loop bounds, descriptors - off the vector register file. Seeing address arithmetic land here rather than in `R` registers is a sign the compiler proved it warp-invariant.

uniformZero.title: URZ - uniform zero register
uniformZero.desc: The uniform datapath's zero register: reads as 0, discards writes.

predicate.title: Predicate register (per-thread)
predicate.desc: One of `P0`-`P7`. A single per-lane bit controlling conditional execution. A guard such as `@P0` runs the instruction only in the lanes where the bit is set - divergence without a branch. `@!P0` inverts it.

predicateTrue.title: PT - true predicate
predicateTrue.desc: Always true. As a guard (`@PT`) it means unconditional; as the incoming operand of a `.AND`-combining compare it is the identity, which is why so many compares end in `, PT`. As a destination it discards the predicate.

uniformPredicate.title: Uniform predicate register
uniformPredicate.desc: One of `UP0`-`UP7`. A single warp-wide predicate bit on the uniform datapath - notably the carry between the halves of a uniform 64-bit add.

special.title: Special register
special.desc: A read-only, system-supplied value reached with `S2R` (or `CS2R` for the cheap constants, `S2UR` when the value is warp-uniform). `S2R` has unknown latency and is scoreboarded, which is why it is issued early and its result consumed much later.

specialZero.title: SRZ - zero special register
specialZero.desc: Reads as zero. `CS2R.64 Rd, SRZ` is the standard idiom for clearing a register pair in one instruction.

barrier.title: Convergence barrier register
barrier.desc: One of `B0`-`B15`. Holds the reconvergence point and participating-lane mask for a divergent region: `BSSY B0, <target>` opens it, `BSYNC B0` reconverges, `BREAK B0` leaves it early. Since Volta these replaced the old implicit reconvergence stack.

scoreboard.title: Scoreboard barrier
scoreboard.desc: One of `SB0`-`SB5`. Tracks an outstanding variable-latency operation (a load, a texture fetch, an `S2R`). The consuming instruction's control code names the barrier it must wait on.

predicateFile.title: PR - the predicate register file
predicateFile.desc: The predicate registers addressed as one value, so that `P2R`/`R2P` can spill all of them to a general register and restore them.

constant.title: Constant memory
constant.desc: `c[bank][offset]` - a read from the constant banks, broadcast to the whole warp and served from a dedicated cache. Effectively free when every lane reads the same address, which is always the case here since the address is an immediate. `cx[URn][offset]` is the *indexed* form, where a uniform register supplies the bank base - how bindless descriptors and dynamically indexed buffers are reached.

attribute.title: Attribute space
attribute.desc: `a[offset]` - the rasterizer's per-pixel interpolant space in a graphics shader, read with `IPA` or `ALD`.

immediate.title: Immediate
immediate.desc: A literal encoded in the instruction. Warp-uniform by construction. Float immediates are printed in decimal, integer and bit-pattern immediates in hex - so `0x3f800000` in a move to a float register is 1.0f.

SR_TID.desc: Thread index within the CTA, packed.

SR_CTAID.desc: CTA index within the grid, packed.

SR_WARPID.desc: Warp slot index within the SM.

SR_SMID.desc: Index of the SM this warp is resident on. Useful for persistent-kernel scheduling; not stable across preemption.

SR_NSMID.desc: Number of SMs on the device.

SR_EQMASK.desc: Mask of lanes whose index equals this lane's.

SR_LTMASK.desc: Mask of lanes with a lower index than this lane - the prefix-sum primitive for warp-aggregated atomics.

SR_LEMASK.desc: Mask of lanes with an index less than or equal to this lane's.

SR_GTMASK.desc: Mask of lanes with a higher index than this lane's.

SR_GEMASK.desc: Mask of lanes with an index greater than or equal to this lane's.

SR_CLOCKLO.desc: Low 32 bits of the SM clock counter.

SR_CLOCKHI.desc: High 32 bits of the SM clock counter.

SR_GLOBALTIMERLO.desc: Low 32 bits of the device-wide nanosecond timer.

SR_GLOBALTIMERHI.desc: High 32 bits of the device-wide nanosecond timer.

SR_INVOCATIONID.desc: Invocation index within a geometry or tessellation stage.

constantBanks._note: Bank 0 is the driver/ABI bank. These offsets are the widely corroborated ones and are heuristics, not a documented layout - the base moves between architectures and between the compute and graphics ABIs. Graphics pipelines additionally use higher banks (c[0x11], c[0x18], ...) for driver tables and descriptor state, which is what `cx[URn][...]` then indexes into.

offsets.0x28: local-memory window base - `MOV R1, c[0x0][0x28]` is the standard stack-pointer prologue

attributeSlots._note: Pixel-shader interpolant space. Position occupies the slots below 0x80 and user varyings start at 0x80; this layout is read off shader disassembly rather than documented.
attributeSlots.0x7c: the interpolated 1/w. `MUFU.RCP` of this slot recovers w, and multiplying an interpolated attribute by that w is the perspective divide - which is why almost every pixel shader opens with `IPA.PASS Rn, a[0x7c]` followed by `MUFU.RCP`. A `noperspective` attribute is recognisable by the *absence* of that sequence.

controlCodeVolta.title: Control code (Volta+)
controlCodeVolta.desc:
Scheduling metadata carried by this instruction itself, decoded from bits [105,126) of the 128-bit encoding by this extension and printed as `[B--2---:R-:W0:Y:S04]`.

The five printed columns run `wait : read : write : yield : stall`. Scoreboards here are **positional and numbered 0-5, exactly as encoded** - one character per scoreboard in the `B` field. Do not read them as the hex mask over barriers 1-6 that Maxwell-era listings and maxas use; that renumbering does not apply to this column.

Scoreboards are counters, not flags: several in-flight instructions can arm the same one, and a wait blocks until it drains to zero.

wait.title: wait mask
wait.desc: Scoreboards that must have drained to zero before this instruction may issue, one slot per scoreboard 0-5. `B--2---` waits on scoreboard 2 alone; `B------` waits on nothing.

read.title: read scoreboard
read.desc: Scoreboard armed until this instruction's *source operands* have been read out, so a later instruction can know when it is safe to overwrite them (WAR protection). `R-` arms none.

write.title: write scoreboard
write.desc: Scoreboard armed until this instruction's *result* has been written back. Used by variable-latency instructions - loads, texture fetches, `S2R` - whose completion time the compiler cannot know. `W-` arms none.

yield.title: yield hint
yield.desc: `Y` hints that the scheduler may switch to another warp after this instruction. This is the raw encoded bit; its polarity is debated among community decoders, so treat it as a hint about the hint.

stall.title: stall count
stall.desc: Cycles the scheduler holds this warp before issuing its next instruction, 0-15, in **decimal** here. Fixed-latency instructions are scheduled entirely by this number - there is no interlock to catch a wrong one.

controlCodeVolta.source: decoded from the instruction encoding by this extension; field layout per arXiv:1903.07486 and community decoders (CuAssembler); cross-checked against nvdisasm's own `.reuse` flags on every dump

controlCode.title: Control code
controlCode.desc:
Scheduling metadata the compiler attaches to each instruction. Through Maxwell these were batched - 8 bytes describing the following three instructions; since Turing each 128-bit instruction carries its own (>=23 bits alongside >=91 bits of opcode and operands).

The five printed columns run `wait : read : write : yield : stall` - the **reverse** of the bitfield order usually quoted (`stall : yield : write : read : wait`). Worth knowing, because reading the columns in the quoted order silently swaps the stall count with the wait mask.

wait.title: wait barrier
wait.desc: Mask of scoreboard barriers this instruction must wait on before it can issue. `06` means barriers 1 and 2.

read.title: read barrier
read.desc: Scoreboard barrier to set when this instruction's *source operands* have been consumed, so they can safely be overwritten.

write.title: write barrier
write.desc: Scoreboard barrier to set when this instruction's *result* is produced. Needed for variable-latency (decoupled) instructions - loads, texture fetches, `S2R` - whose completion time the compiler cannot know.

yield.title: yield hint
yield.desc: `Y` hints that the scheduler may switch to another warp here. Switching warps is normally free.

stall.title: stall count
stall.desc: Cycles to stall after this instruction, 0-15, in hex. **0 means dual-issue with the next instruction.** Fixed-latency (coupled) instructions are scheduled entirely by this number - there is no interlock to catch a wrong one.

controlCode.source: slides; column order derived from the worked examples in the slides; instruction-width detail from arXiv:1903.07486
